ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a regular decagon, and a diagonal is drawn from the top vertex to a lower-right vertex. This diagonal cuts out a small quadrilateral on the right side; along the boundary of the decagon, the small quadrilateral contains in order the top vertex, the two adjacent vertices on the upper right, and the lower-right endpoint of the diagonal. Angle x is marked at the lower-right endpoint of the diagonal, and is the angle between the diagonal and the right vertical side. Then reason: According to the method, label the upper endpoint of the diagonal as A, the lower endpoint as D, and the two middle decagon vertices on the right side in order as B, C, then the small region is quadrilateral A-B-C-D, and x is the angle of the quadrilateral at D. Each interior angle of a regular decagon is (10-2)×180/10 = 144°. In the figure B is a vertex of the original regular decagon, so ∠B = 144°. All vertices of a regular decagon are concyclic, therefore A, B, C, D form a cyclic quadrilateral, and opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, so x + 144° = 180°. Therefore x = 36°.

raw_record.question_text:

<image1>

method.method_draft: Label the diagonal endpoints as the top vertex A and the lower-right vertex D, and label the two intervening right-side decagon vertices B and C, so the small region is quadrilateral A-B-C-D with x at D. From the text, the outside polygon is a regular decagon, so each interior angle is (10-2)180/10 = 144 degrees. From the image, angle B is one of the original decagon interior angles and is opposite x in the quadrilateral. Since all vertices of a regular decagon lie on one circle, A-B-C-D is a cyclic quadrilateral, so opposite angles are supplementary. Thus x = 180 - 144 = 36 degrees.
